newsitem.title: USA: Lucent creates voice/video via Web venture.
newsitem.headline: Lucent creates voice/video via Web venture.

text.p: Lucent Technologies Inc. said Tuesday it has set up a new software group to provide businesses and consumers with high-quality voice, music and video transmission over intranets and the Internet.

The group, called elemedia (short for elements for multimedia), will sell voice software, which enables "telephone quality" conversations over the Internet. Other products will include speakerphone software, which grants full, two-way conversational capabilities to personal computers and Internet phone devices.
By the next quarter, the former AT&T Corp. equipment unit said the venture's software will enable home and business-quality videoconferencing over the Internet.
In addition, Lucent plans to offer FM stereo/compact-disc quality audio software to enable services like music-on-demand and real-time audio broadcasting over networks, it said.

"We're capitalising on more than a decade of Bell Laboratories software research and development in packet technologies to bring Internet telephony to the level of quality people are accustomed to," said Joe Mele, president of elemedia.

Packet technologies refers to the standard method of sending data over networks by breaking it into small packages of electronic bits on the sender's end of a transmission and reassembling the packages on the receiving end.
However, this transmission method has severe limitations when used to send real-time voice or video images.
Voice or video communications typically have a jerky, degraded quality when transmitted via the packet delivery method.

Lucent said its technology would resolve such drawbacks, allowing for high-quality voice or image transmission over the Internet that could compete with conventional methods of telephone and broadcast video transmission.
Bell Laboratories is the research and development arm of the Murray Hill, N.J.-based company.
"This software will help move voice, music and video over the Internet beyond the current base of technologists and hobbyists and into the mainstream," Mele said.

The package of products, to be sold under the Media Plus family name, will include software components that are designed so software vendors, Internet service providers and other companies can integrate them easily into products and services they provide to customers.

Initial customers include Camelot Corp., maker of the DigiPhone Internet telephony software; Isochrone, a developer of Internet communications software applications; and Soundprint Media Centre, a provider of Internet services for the public radio broadcasting industry.
The elemedia group is the second business venture created by Lucent to market Bell Labs software innovations.

Lucent was formed as a result of AT&T's previously announced plans to restructure itself into three separate companies. Lucent designs, builds and delivers a wide range of public and private networks, communications systems and software, consumer and business telephone systems and microelectronics components.

Under terms of its spin-off from AT&T, Lucent retained control of Bell Laboratories, AT&T's research arm, which over the decades has been responsible for many of the key innovations that form the core of both the modern telephone system and the Internet.
Lucent's stock rose 37.5 cents to $39.875 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-morning.
